sanskrit: kṛttottamāṅgās te rājan bhallaiḥ śatasahasraśaḥ apatan rudhirārdrāṅgā nikṛttā iva kiṃśukāḥ
english: Their heads severed by his broad-headed arrows, O king, they fell in their hundreds and thousands, their limbs drenched in blood, like kiṃśuka trees cut down.

sanskrit: hateṣu teṣu sarveṣu vītahavyaḥ suteṣv atha prādravan nagaraṃ hitvā bhṛgor āśramam apy uta
english: When all those sons were slain, Vītahavya fled, abandoning his city, and made his way even to the hermitage of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: yayau bhṛguṃ ca śaraṇaṃ vītahavyo narādhipaḥ abhayaṃ ca dadau tasmai rājñe rājan bhṛgus tathā tato dadāv āsanaṃ ca tasmai śiṣyo bhṛgos tadā
english: The king Vītahavya went to Bhṛgu for refuge, and Bhṛgu, O king, granted that king his protection; then, becoming Bhṛgu's disciple, he was offered a seat as well.

sanskrit: athānupadam evāśu tatrāgacchat pratardanaḥ sa prāpya cāśramapadaṃ divodāsātmajo 'bravīt
english: Then, hard upon his heels, Pratardana swiftly arrived there; and reaching the precincts of the hermitage, the son of Divodāsa spoke.

sanskrit: bho bhoḥ ke 'trāśrame santi bhṛgoḥ śiṣyā mahātmanaḥ draṣṭum icche munim ahaṃ tasyācakṣata mām iti
english: "Ho there! Who are present in this hermitage as disciples of the great-souled Bhṛgu? I wish to see the sage; announce me to him."

sanskrit: sa taṃ viditvā tu bhṛgur niścakrāmāśramāt tadā pūjayām āsa ca tato vidhinā parameṇa ha
english: When Bhṛgu learned of him, he came forth from the hermitage and honored him then with the highest ceremony.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ rājendra kiṃ kāryam iti pārthivam sa covāca nṛpas tasmai yad āgamanakāraṇam
english: And he said to that prince, O lord of kings, "What is your purpose?" And the king told him the reason for his coming.

sanskrit: ayaṃ brahmann ito rājā vītahavyo visarjyatām asya putrair hi me brahman kṛtsno vaṃśaḥ praṇāśitaḥ utsāditaś ca viṣayaḥ kāśīnāṃ ratnasaṃcayaḥ
english: "This king Vītahavya, O brahman, let him be given up from here; for by his sons, O brahman, my whole lineage was destroyed, and the realm of the Kāśis with its store of treasures was laid waste."

sanskrit: etasya vīryadṛptasya hataṃ putraśataṃ mayā asyedānīṃ vadhād brahman bhaviṣyāmy anṛṇaḥ pituḥ
english: "The hundred sons of this man, drunk with his might, were slain by me; now by his death, O brahman, I shall become free of my debt to my father."

sanskrit: tam uvāca kṛpāviṣṭo bhṛgur dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ nehāsti kṣatriyaḥ kaś cit sarve hīme dvijātayaḥ
english: To him Bhṛgu, foremost of the upholders of dharma, filled with compassion, said: "There is no kṣatriya here at all; for all these are brahmans."

sanskrit: evaṃ tu vacanaṃ śrutvā bhṛgos tathyaṃ pratardanaḥ pādāv upaspṛśya śanaiḥ prahasan vākyam abravīt
english: Hearing this truthful word of Bhṛgu, Pratardana gently touched his feet and, smiling, spoke these words:

sanskrit: evam apy asmi bhagavan kṛtakṛtyo na saṃśayaḥ yad eṣa rājā vīryeṇa svajātiṃ tyājito mayā
english: "Even so, O blessed one, I have accomplished my purpose, without doubt, since by my prowess this king has been made to forsake his own caste."

sanskrit: anujānīhi māṃ brahman dhyāyasva ca śivena mām tyājito hi mayā jātim eṣa rājā bhṛgūdvaha
english: "Give me leave, O brahman, and think of me with kindly intent; for by me this king has been made to lose his caste, O scion of Bhṛgu."

sanskrit: tatas tenābhyanujñāto yayau rājā pratardanaḥ yathāgataṃ mahārāja muktvā viṣam ivoragaḥ
english: Then, granted leave by him, King Pratardana departed as he had come, O great king, like a serpent that has discharged its venom.

sanskrit: bhṛgor vacanamātreṇa sa ca brahmarṣitāṃ gataḥ vītahavyo mahārāja brahmavāditvam eva ca
english: And by the mere word of Bhṛgu, Vītahavya attained, O great king, the state of a brahman seer and the mastery of brahman-lore.

sanskrit: tasya gṛtsamadaḥ putro rūpeṇendra ivāparaḥ śakras tvam iti yo daityair nigṛhītaḥ kilābhavat
english: His son was Gṛtsamada, in beauty like a second Indra, who was once seized by the Daityas with the cry, "You are Śakra!"

sanskrit: ṛgvede vartate cāgryā śrutir atra viśāṃ pate yatra gṛtsamado brahman brāhmaṇaiḥ sa mahīyate
english: And there is a foremost sacred text in this regard in the Ṛgveda, O lord of peoples, wherein that Gṛtsamada, O brahman, is exalted by the brahmans.

sanskrit: sa brahmacārī viprarṣiḥ śrīmān gṛtsamado 'bhavat putro gṛtsamadasyāpi sucetā abhavad dvijaḥ
english: That Gṛtsamada became a celibate brahman seer, illustrious; and Gṛtsamada's son too was a brahman named Sucetas.

sanskrit: varcāḥ sutejasaḥ putro vihavyas tasya cātmajaḥ vihavyasya tu putras tu vitatyas tasya cātmajaḥ
english: Varcas was the son of the mighty-splendored one, and Vihavya was his offspring; Vihavya's son was Vitatya, and his offspring in turn.

sanskrit: vitatyasya sutaḥ satyaḥ santaḥ satyasya cātmajaḥ śravās tasya sutaś carṣiḥ śravasaś cābhavat tamaḥ
english: Vitatya's son was Satya, and Santa was Satya's offspring; his son was the seer Śravas, and from Śravas came Tamas.

sanskrit: tamasaś ca prakāśo 'bhūt tanayo dvijasattamaḥ prakāśasya ca vāgindro babhūva jayatāṃ varaḥ
english: And from Tamas was born a son, Prakāśa, best of the twice-born; and from Prakāśa came Vāgindra, foremost of the victorious.

sanskrit: tasyātmajaś ca pramatir vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ ghṛtācyāṃ tasya putras tu rurur nāmodapadyata
english: His son was Pramati, master of the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas; and to him by Ghṛtācī was born a son named Ruru.

sanskrit: pramadvarāyāṃ tu ruroḥ putraḥ samudapadyata śunako nāma viprarṣir yasya putro 'tha śaunakaḥ
english: And to Ruru by Pramadvarā was born a son, a brahman seer named Śunaka, whose son in turn was Śaunaka.

sanskrit: evaṃ vipratvam agamad vītahavyo narādhipaḥ bhṛgoḥ prasādād rājendra kṣatriyaḥ kṣatriyarṣabha
english: Thus did the king Vītahavya attain to brahman-hood, by the grace of Bhṛgu, O lord of kings, though a kṣatriya, O bull among kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: tathaiva kathito vaṃśo mayā gārtsamadas tava vistareṇa mahārāja kim anyad anupṛcchasi
english: So too has the lineage of Gṛtsamada been recounted by me to you in full, O great king. What else do you ask?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ke pūjyāḥ ke namaskāryā mānavair bharatarṣabha vistareṇa tad ācakṣva na hi tṛpyāmi kathyatām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Who are to be honored, who are to be reverenced by men, O bull of the Bharatas? Tell me this in full, for I am not sated; let it be told.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nāradasya ca saṃvādaṃ vāsudevasya cobhayoḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount this ancient tale, the dialogue of the two, Nārada and Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: nāradaṃ prāñjaliṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjayānaṃ dvijarṣabhān keśavaḥ paripapraccha bhagavan kān namasyasi
english: Seeing Nārada with joined palms doing honor to the bulls among the twice-born, Keśava asked him: "Blessed one, whom do you reverence?"

sanskrit: bahumānaḥ paraḥ keṣu bhavato yān namasyasi śakyaṃ cec chrotum icchāmi brūhy etad dharmavittama
english: "Toward whom is your highest regard, those whom you reverence? If it may be heard, I wish to know; tell me this, O best of the knowers of dharma."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca śṛṇu govinda yān etān pūjayāmy arimardana tvatto 'nyaḥ kaḥ pumāṃl loke śrotum etad ihārhati
english: Nārada said: Hear, O Govinda, those whom I honor, O crusher of foes; for what man in the world other than you is worthy to hear this here?

sanskrit: varuṇaṃ vāyum ādityaṃ parjanyaṃ jātavedasam sthāṇuṃ skandaṃ tathā lakṣmīṃ viṣṇuṃ brahmāṇam eva ca
english: Varuṇa, Vāyu, the Sun, Parjanya, the fire-born Jātavedas, Sthāṇu, Skanda, and Lakṣmī, Viṣṇu and Brahmā too—

sanskrit: vācaspatiṃ candramasam apaḥ pṛthvīṃ sarasvatīm satataṃ ye namasyanti tān namasyāmy ahaṃ vibho
english: Vācaspati, the Moon, the Waters, the Earth, and Sarasvatī—those who reverence these unceasingly, them do I reverence, O mighty one.

sanskrit: tapodhanān vedavido nityaṃ vedaparāyaṇān mahārhān vṛṣṇiśārdūla sadā saṃpūjayāmy aham
english: Those rich in austerity, knowers of the Veda, ever devoted to the Veda, most worthy—O tiger of the Vṛṣṇis, them I always honor.

sanskrit: abhuktvā devakāryāṇi kurvate ye 'vikatthanāḥ saṃtuṣṭāś ca kṣamāyuktās tān namasyāmy ahaṃ vibho
english: Those who, before eating, perform the rites of the gods, free of boastfulness, content and endowed with forbearance—them I reverence, O mighty one.

sanskrit: samyag dadati ye ceṣṭān kṣāntā dāntā jitendriyāḥ sasyaṃ dhanaṃ kṣitiṃ gāś ca tān namasyāmi yādava
english: Those who give rightly to the worthy—patient, self-controlled, masters of their senses—grain, wealth, land, and cattle, them I reverence, O Yādava.

sanskrit: ye te tapasi vartante vane mūlaphalāśanāḥ asaṃcayāḥ kriyāvantas tān namasyāmi yādava
english: Those who dwell in austerity in the forest, feeding on roots and fruits, hoarding nothing, performing their rites—them I reverence, O Yādava.

sanskrit: ye bhṛtyabharaṇe saktāḥ satataṃ cātithipriyāḥ bhuñjante devaśeṣāṇi tān namasyāmi yādava
english: Those intent upon supporting their dependents, ever fond of guests, who eat what remains after offering to the gods—them I reverence, O Yādava.

sanskrit: ye vedaṃ prāpya durdharṣā vāgmino brahmavādinaḥ yājanādhyāpane yuktā nityaṃ tān pūjayāmy aham
english: Those who, having mastered the Veda, are unassailable, eloquent, expounders of the brahman, ever engaged in performing sacrifices and in teaching—them I honor.

sanskrit: prasannahṛdayāś caiva sarvasattveṣu nityaśaḥ ā pṛṣṭhatāpāt svādhyāye yuktās tān pūjayāmy aham
english: And those of serene heart toward all beings always, devoted to their study even to the point of bodily exhaustion—them I honor.

sanskrit: guruprasāde svādhyāye yatante ye sthiravratāḥ śuśrūṣavo 'nasūyantas tān namasyāmi yādava
english: Those who strive for the favor of their teacher and for their study, steadfast in their vows, eager to serve and free of envy—them I reverence, O Yādava.

sanskrit: suvratā munayo ye ca brahmaṇyāḥ satyasaṃgarāḥ voḍhāro havyakavyānāṃ tān namasyāmi yādava
english: Those sages of good vows, devoted to the brahman, true to their pledges, bearers of offerings to gods and ancestors—them I reverence, O Yādava.

sanskrit: bhaikṣyacaryāsu niratāḥ kṛśā gurukulāśrayāḥ niḥsukhā nirdhanā ye ca tān namasyāmi yādava
english: Those devoted to the practice of begging, lean, sheltering in the teacher's house, without comfort and without wealth—them I reverence, O Yādava.

sanskrit: nirmamā niṣpratidvaṃdvā nirhrīkā niṣprayojanāḥ ahiṃsāniratā ye ca ye ca satyavratā narāḥ dāntāḥ śamaparāś caiva tān namasyāmi keśava
english: Free of possessiveness, free of rivalry, free of false shame, free of selfish ends, devoted to non-injury, and those men vowed to truth, self-controlled and intent on tranquillity—them I reverence, O Keśava.

sanskrit: devatātithipūjāyāṃ prasaktā gṛhamedhinaḥ kapotavṛttayo nityaṃ tān namasyāmi yādava
english: Householders devoted to the worship of gods and guests, who live always like the dove, gleaning only what suffices—them I reverence, O Yādava.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ trivargaḥ kṛtyeṣu vartate nopahīyate śiṣṭācārapravṛttāś ca tān namasyāmy ahaṃ sadā
english: Those in whose deeds the three aims of life abide and are not diminished, who follow the conduct of the cultivated—them I reverence always.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇās triṣu lokeṣu ye trivargam anuṣṭhitāḥ alolupāḥ puṇyaśīlās tān namasyāmi keśava
english: Those brahmans in the three worlds who pursue the three aims of life, free of greed, of holy character—them I reverence, O Keśava.

sanskrit: abbhakṣā vāyubhakṣāś ca sudhābhakṣāś ca ye sadā vrataiś ca vividhair yuktās tān namasyāmi mādhava
english: Those who feed always on water, on air, or on nectar, and who are bound by various vows—them I reverence, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: ayonīn agniyonīṃś ca brahmayonīṃs tathaiva ca sarvabhūtātmayonīṃś ca tān namasyāmy ahaṃ dvijān
english: Those of no womb, those born of fire, those born of the brahman, and those born of the self that is the source of all beings—those twice-born I reverence.

sanskrit: nityam etān namasyāmi kṛṣṇa lokakarān ṛṣīn lokajyeṣṭhāñ jñānaniṣṭhāṃs tamoghnāṃl lokabhāskarān
english: These I reverence always, O Kṛṣṇa—the seers who make the worlds, eldest of the worlds, fixed in knowledge, destroyers of darkness, lights of the world.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam api vārṣṇeya dvijān pūjaya nityadā pūjitāḥ pūjanārhā hi sukhaṃ dāsyanti te 'nagha
english: Therefore you too, O scion of the Vṛṣṇis, honor the twice-born always; for when honored, those worthy of honor will grant you happiness, O sinless one.

sanskrit: asmiṃl loke sadā hy ete paratra ca sukhapradāḥ ta ete mānyamānā vai pradāsyanti sukhaṃ tava
english: For in this world and in the next these are ever givers of happiness; honored as they deserve, they will indeed bestow happiness upon you.

sanskrit: ye sarvātithayo nityaṃ goṣu ca brāhmaṇeṣu ca nityaṃ satye ca niratā durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: Those who are ever hospitable to all, devoted always to cattle and to brahmans and to truth—they pass beyond all hardships.

sanskrit: nityaṃ śamaparā ye ca tathā ye cānasūyakāḥ nityaṃ svādhyāyino ye ca durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: Those ever intent on tranquillity, and those free of envy, and those ever devoted to their study—they pass beyond all hardships.

sanskrit: sarvān devān namasyanti ye caikaṃ devam āśritāḥ śraddadhānāś ca dāntāś ca durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: Those who reverence all the gods while relying upon a single god, full of faith and self-controlled—they pass beyond all hardships.

sanskrit: tathaiva viprapravarān namaskṛtya yatavratān bhavanti ye dānaratā durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: And likewise those who, having reverenced the foremost brahmans of disciplined vows, become devoted to giving—they pass beyond all hardships.

sanskrit: agnīn ādhāya vidhivat prayatā dhārayanti ye prāptāḥ somāhutiṃ caiva durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: Those who, having established the sacred fires according to rule, maintain them with care and have attained the soma-offering—they pass beyond all hardships.

sanskrit: mātāpitror guruṣu ca samyag vartanti ye sadā yathā tvaṃ vṛṣṇiśārdūlety uktvaivaṃ virarāma saḥ
english: Those who always conduct themselves rightly toward mother and father and teachers, just as you do, O tiger of the Vṛṣṇis—so saying, he fell silent.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam api kaunteya pitṛdevadvijātithīn samyak pūjaya yena tvaṃ gatim iṣṭām avāpsyasi
english: Therefore you too, O son of Kuntī, rightly honor ancestors, gods, the twice-born, and guests, by which you shall attain the goal you desire.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ rājñaḥ sarvakṛtyānāṃ garīyaḥ syāt pitāmaha kiṃ kurvan karma nṛpatir ubhau lokau samaśnute
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of all a king's duties, which is the weightiest, O grandsire? By doing what deed does a king win both worlds?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etad rājñaḥ kṛtyatamam abhiṣiktasya bhārata brāhmaṇānām anuṣṭhānam atyantaṃ sukham icchatā śrotriyān brāhmaṇān vṛddhān nityam evābhipūjayet
english: Bhīṣma said: This is the foremost duty of a consecrated king, O Bhārata: the serving of brahmans. One who desires the highest happiness should ever honor the learned, the brahmans, and the aged.

sanskrit: paurajānapadāṃś cāpi brāhmaṇāṃś ca bahuśrutān sāntvena bhogadānena namaskārais tathārcayet
english: And the brahmans of city and countryside, deeply learned, he should honor with conciliating words, with gifts of enjoyments, and with marks of reverence.

sanskrit: etat kṛtyatamaṃ rājño nityam eveti lakṣayet yathātmānaṃ yathā putrāṃs tathaitān paripālayet
english: He should mark this as ever the foremost duty of a king; he should cherish them as he would himself, as he would his own sons.

sanskrit: ye cāpy eṣāṃ pūjyatamās tān dṛḍhaṃ pratipūjayet teṣu śānteṣu tad rāṣṭraṃ sarvam eva virājate
english: And those among them who are most worthy of honor he should honor steadfastly; when they are at peace, the whole realm shines forth.

sanskrit: te pūjyās te namaskāryās te rakṣyāḥ pitaro yathā teṣv eva yātrā lokasya bhūtānām iva vāsave
english: They are to be honored, they to be reverenced, they to be guarded like one's own fathers; upon them rests the world's course, as upon Vāsava that of beings.

sanskrit: abhicārair upāyaiś ca daheyur api tejasā niḥśeṣaṃ kupitāḥ kuryur ugrāḥ satyaparākramāḥ
english: By sorceries and by stratagems, even by their own fiery power, they could consume; when angered, the fierce ones, whose valor is truth, could leave nothing remaining.

sanskrit: nāntam eṣāṃ prapaśyāmi na diśaś cāpy apāvṛtāḥ kupitāḥ samudīkṣante dāveṣv agniśikhā iva
english: I see no limit to their power, nor any quarter left uncovered; when angered they blaze up like flames of fire in a forest conflagration.

sanskrit: vidyan teṣāṃ sāhasikā guṇās teṣām atīva hi kūpā iva tṛṇacchannā viśuddhā dyaur ivāpare
english: There are found in them daring qualities in the extreme; some are like wells covered over with grass, while others are pure as the sky.

sanskrit: prasahyakāriṇaḥ ke cit kārpāsamṛdavo 'pare santi caiṣām atiśaṭhās tathānye 'titapasvinaḥ
english: Some among them act by force, others are soft as cotton; some of them are exceedingly crafty, while still others are exceeding ascetics.

sanskrit: kṛṣigorakṣyam apy anye bhaikṣam anye 'py anuṣṭhitāḥ corāś cānye 'nṛtāś cānye tathānye naṭanartakāḥ
english: Some practice farming and the tending of cattle, others live by begging; some are thieves, others liars, and yet others actors and dancers.

sanskrit: sarvakarmasu dṛśyante praśānteṣv itareṣu ca vividhācārayuktāś ca brāhmaṇā bharatarṣabha
english: They are seen in all occupations, the peaceful and the other kind, and endowed with manifold ways of life are the brahmans, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: nānākarmasu yuktānāṃ bahukarmopajīvinām dharmajñānāṃ satāṃ teṣāṃ nityam evānukīrtayet
english: Engaged though they are in diverse occupations and living by many trades, they are knowers of dharma and good men; their praise one should ever proclaim.

sanskrit: pitṝṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca manuṣyoragarakṣasām purohitā mahābhāgā brāhmaṇā vai narādhipa
english: Of ancestors and of gods, of men, serpents, and rākṣasas, the brahmans, O lord of men, are the highly blessed household priests.

sanskrit: naite devair na pitṛbhir na gandharvair na rākṣasaiḥ nāsurair na piśācaiś ca śakyā jetuṃ dvijātayaḥ
english: These twice-born cannot be conquered by gods, nor by ancestors, nor by gandharvas, nor by rākṣasas, nor by asuras, nor by piśācas.

sanskrit: adaivaṃ daivataṃ kuryur daivataṃ cāpy adaivatam yam iccheyuḥ sa rājā syād yaṃ dviṣyuḥ sa parābhavet
english: They could make a non-god into a god, and a god into a non-god; whomever they wish, he becomes king, and whomever they hate, he comes to ruin.

sanskrit: parivādaṃ ca ye kuryur brāhmaṇānām acetasaḥ nindāpraśaṃsākuśalāḥ kīrtyakīrtiparāvarāḥ parikupyanti te rājan satataṃ dviṣatāṃ dvijāḥ
english: And those senseless ones who utter reproach against the brahmans—the twice-born, skilled in blame and praise, who dispense fame and infamy, high and low, grow ever wrathful, O king, toward those who hate them.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā yaṃ praśaṃsanti puruṣaḥ sa pravardhate brāhmaṇair yaḥ parākruṣṭaḥ parābhūyāt kṣaṇād dhi saḥ
english: The man whom the brahmans praise, that man prospers; but he who is reviled by the brahmans comes to ruin in an instant.

sanskrit: śakā yavanakāmbojās tās tāḥ kṣatriyajātayaḥ vṛṣalatvaṃ parigatā brāhmaṇānām adarśanāt
english: The Śakas, Yavanas, and Kāmbojas, and those various kṣatriya races, have fallen into the condition of degraded men through the absence of brahmans.

sanskrit: dramiḷāś ca kaliṅgāś ca pulindāś cāpy uśīnarāḥ kaulāḥ sarpā māhiṣakās tās tāḥ kṣatriyajātayaḥ
english: The Dramiḷas and Kaliṅgas, the Pulindas and Uśīnaras, the Kaulas, Sarpas, and Māhiṣakas—those various kṣatriya races—

sanskrit: vṛṣalatvaṃ parigatā brāhmaṇānām adarśanāt śreyān parājayas tebhyo na jayo jayatāṃ vara
english: have fallen into the condition of degraded men through the absence of brahmans. Better is defeat at their hands than victory, O best of the victorious.

sanskrit: yas tu sarvam idaṃ hanyād brāhmaṇaṃ ca na tatsamam brahmavadhyā mahān doṣa ity āhuḥ paramarṣayaḥ
english: Even one who should slay all this world—there is nothing equal to slaying a brahman; the killing of a brahman is a grievous sin, so say the supreme seers.
